summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint on install
details: The package is a shim under the @ecg-internal scope with no real functionality — index.js exports a Proxy that returns no-op functions for any accessed property. Its only effect is to execute beacon.cjs, which runs both from the declared postinstall script ("node beacon.cjs") and on require of index.js. beacon.cjs collects host identifiers — os.hostname(), __dirname (install path), process.cwd(), and the Node version — and POSTs them as JSON to the hardcoded bare-IP plaintext HTTP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc. The scope name @ecg-internal combined with an empty-functionality shim and a bare-IP callback is the canonical dependency-confusion reconnaissance pattern: publishing an internal-looking name to the public registry so that misconfigured resolvers inside a target organization install it and beacon back host and path details confirming the private name is reachable.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
